verses.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to God’s chosen people living as foreigners scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,
chosen according to the foreknowledge of God the Father, made holy by the Spirit, to obey Jesus Christ and be sprinkled with his blood: May grace and peace increase for you.
Praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ! In his great mercy he gave us new birth into a living hope through Jesus Christ’s resurrection from the dead,
and into an inheritance that can never decay, spoil, or fade. It’s kept in heaven for you,
who are protected by God’s power through faith for the salvation ready to be revealed in the last time.
Because of this, you celebrate, even though for a little while you may have to suffer grief in all kinds of trials.

These trials show that your faith is genuine. It’s more valuable than gold, which can be destroyed even though it’s tested by fire. Your faith will bring praise, glory, and honor when Jesus Christ is revealed.
You love him even though you haven’t seen him. Though you don’t see him now, you believe in him and celebrate with a joy too glorious for words,
because you’re receiving the goal of your faith: the salvation of your souls.
The prophets searched carefully and investigated this salvation. They prophesied about the grace meant for you,
trying to learn when and in what circumstances the Spirit of Christ in them was pointing when he predicted Christ’s sufferings and the glories that would follow.

They were shown that they weren’t serving themselves but you, when they spoke about the things now announced to you by those who preached the good news through the Holy Spirit sent from heaven. Even angels long to look into these things.
So prepare your minds for action, stay clearheaded, and set your hope completely on the grace you’ll receive when Jesus Christ is revealed.
As obedient children, don’t let your old desires shape you, the desires you had when you lived in ignorance.
Instead, just as the one who called you is holy, be holy in everything you do,
because Scripture says, “Be holy, because I am holy.”
Since you call on a Father who judges everyone’s work impartially, live with reverent respect during your time as foreigners here.
You know you weren’t bought back from the empty way of life handed down by your ancestors with things that perish, like silver or gold,
but with Christ’s precious blood, like that of a spotless lamb without defect.
He was chosen before the creation of the world, but was revealed in these last times for your sake.
Through him you believe in God, who raised him from the dead and gave him glory, so your faith and hope are in God.
Now that you’ve purified yourselves by obeying the truth, so that you have sincere love for your brothers and sisters, love one another deeply from the heart.
You’ve been born again, not from seed that perishes, but from seed that can’t perish, through God’s living and lasting word.
For, “All people are like grass, and all their glory is like the flowers of the field; the grass withers and the flowers fall,
but the Lord’s word lasts forever.” This is the word that was preached to you as good news.
So get rid of all malice, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and every kind of slander.
Like newborn babies, crave pure spiritual milk, so that by it you may grow up into salvation,
since you’ve tasted that the Lord is good.
Come to him, the living Stone—rejected by people but chosen and precious to God—
and, like living stones, let yourselves be built into a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, offering spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ.
For Scripture says: “Look, I lay a chosen and precious cornerstone in Zion, and whoever trusts in him will never be put to shame.”
So, for you who believe, this stone is precious. But for those who don’t believe: “The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone,”
and, “A stone that makes people stumble, a rock that makes them fall.” They stumble because they disobey the word, which is also what they were destined for.
But you are a chosen people, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God’s own people, so you can declare the praises of the one who called you out of darkness into his wonderful light.
Once you weren’t a people, but now you’re God’s people. Once you had received no mercy, but now you’ve received mercy.
Dear friends, I urge you, as foreigners and temporary residents, to stay away from sinful desires that wage war against your soul.
Live such good lives among the nations that, though they accuse you of doing wrong, they may see your good deeds and honor God on the day he visits us.
For the Lord’s sake, submit to every human authority, whether to the emperor as the highest authority,
or to governors sent by him to punish wrongdoers and commend those who do right.
For God wants you to silence the ignorance of foolish people by doing good.
Live as free people, but don’t use your freedom to cover up evil. Live as God’s servants.
Honor everyone. Love the family of believers. Fear God. Honor the emperor.
Household servants, submit to your masters with all respect—not only to those who are good and considerate, but also to those who are harsh.
It’s commendable if someone bears up under unjust suffering because they’re conscious of God.
What credit is there in enduring a beating for doing wrong? But if you suffer for doing good and endure it, that’s commendable before God.
You were called to this, because Christ suffered for you and left you an example, so you could follow in his steps.
“He committed no sin, and no deceit was found in his mouth.”
When he was insulted, he didn’t insult back; when he suffered, he didn’t threaten. Instead, he entrusted himself to the one who judges justly.
He himself carried our sins in his body on the cross, so we could die to sins and live for righteousness. By his wounds you’ve been healed.
You were like sheep wandering away, but now you’ve returned to the Shepherd and Guardian of your souls.
In the same way, wives, submit to your own husbands, so that if any of them don’t believe the word, they may be won over without words by the way you live,
when they see your pure and respectful conduct.
Your beauty shouldn’t come from outward things like elaborate hairstyles, gold jewelry, or fine clothes.
Instead, let it come from your inner self: the lasting beauty of a gentle and quiet spirit, which is precious to God.
That’s how the holy women of the past who put their hope in God made themselves beautiful. They submitted to their own husbands,
like Sarah, who obeyed Abraham and called him her lord. You are her daughters if you do what is right and don’t give in to fear.
In the same way, husbands, live with your wives thoughtfully and honor them as the more delicate partner and as fellow heirs of the gift of life, so that nothing will block your prayers.
Finally, all of you, be united in purpose, sympathetic, loving as family, tenderhearted, and humble.
Don’t repay evil with evil or insult with insult. Instead, repay them with blessing, because you were called to inherit a blessing.
“For whoever wants to love life and see good days must keep their tongue from evil and their lips from deceitful speech.
They must turn from evil and do good; they must seek peace and pursue it.
For the Lord’s eyes are on the righteous, and his ears are open to their prayer. But the Lord opposes those who do evil.”
Who can harm you if you’re eager to do what’s good?
But even if you suffer for doing what’s right, you’re blessed. Don’t be afraid of their threats or intimidated.
Instead, honor Christ as Lord in your hearts. Always be ready to give an answer to anyone who asks why you have this hope. Do it with gentleness and respect,
keeping a clear conscience, so that those who insult your good behavior in Christ will be ashamed of their slander.
It’s better, if it’s God’s will, to suffer for doing good than for doing evil.
Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring you to God. He was put to death in the body but made alive in the spirit.
In the spirit he also went and made a proclamation to the spirits in prison,
who disobeyed long ago when God patiently waited in Noah’s days while the ark was being built. In it, a few people—eight altogether—were saved through water.
That water symbolizes baptism, which now saves you—not as a removal of dirt from the body, but as a pledge to God from a good conscience. It saves you through Jesus Christ’s resurrection,
who has gone into heaven and is at God’s right hand, with angels, authorities, and powers under his rule.
Since Christ suffered in his body, arm yourselves with the same attitude. Whoever suffers in the body is done with sin,
so they don’t spend the rest of their earthly life chasing human desires, but live for God’s will.
You’ve already spent enough time doing what the nations choose to do: living wildly, chasing desires, getting drunk, partying, drinking hard, and worshiping idols.
They’re surprised you don’t plunge into the same flood of reckless living, and they insult you.
But they’ll have to answer to the one ready to judge the living and the dead.
That’s why the good news was preached even to those who are now dead, so that though they were judged in the body as people are, they could live in the spirit as God does.
The end of all things is near. So be clearheaded and self-controlled so you can pray.
Above all, keep loving one another deeply, because love covers many sins.
Welcome one another without complaining.
Each of you should use whatever gift you’ve received to serve others, as faithful stewards of God’s varied grace.

If anyone speaks, let it be as someone speaking God’s words. If anyone serves, let it be with the strength God provides, so that God may be praised in everything through Jesus Christ. Glory and power belong to him forever and ever. Amen.
Dear friends, don’t be surprised by the fiery trial happening among you to test you, as if something strange were happening.
Instead, rejoice that you share in Christ’s sufferings, so you can be overjoyed when his glory is revealed.
If you’re insulted because of Christ’s name, you’re blessed, because the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you.
None of you should suffer as a murderer, thief, criminal, or meddler.
But if you suffer as a Christian, don’t be ashamed. Praise God that you bear that name.
For the time has come for judgment to begin with God’s household. If it begins with us, what will the outcome be for those who don’t obey God’s good news?
“If it’s hard for the righteous to be saved, what will happen to the ungodly and the sinner?”
So those who suffer according to God’s will should entrust themselves to their faithful Creator and keep doing good.
I appeal to the elders among you, as a fellow elder and witness of Christ’s sufferings, who will also share in the glory about to be revealed:
Care for God’s flock among you, watching over them—not because you have to, but willingly, as God wants; not for greedy gain, but eagerly;
not bossing around those entrusted to you, but being examples to the flock.
And when the Chief Shepherd appears, you’ll receive the crown of glory that never fades.
In the same way, younger people, submit to the elders. All of you, clothe yourselves with humility toward one another, because “God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
So humble yourselves under God’s mighty hand, so he may lift you up at the right time.
Throw all your worries on him, because he cares about you.
Stay alert and clearheaded. Your enemy the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour.
Stand firm against him in faith, knowing that believers throughout the world are going through the same kinds of suffering.
After you’ve suffered for a little while, the God of all grace, who called you to his eternal glory in Christ, will restore you, make you strong, and set you firmly in place.
To him be power forever. Amen.
I’ve written briefly to you through Silvanus, whom I consider a faithful brother. I want to encourage you and testify that this is the true grace of God. Stand firm in it.
The church in Babylon, chosen together with you, sends greetings, and so does my son Mark.
Greet one another with a kiss of love. Peace to all of you who are in Christ.
